question: Should QQBot expose `QQBOT_DATA_DIR` as a second filesystem contract after active state moved to SQLite under `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and if so should it cover only legacy and download paths?
rationale: The linked bug is real, but the durable product contract cannot be inferred from the helper patch: current main separates canonical SQLite state, media roots, and legacy/download paths, while repository policy sets a high bar for new environment variables.

options.title: Keep one state contract
options.body: Remove the new variable, update the misleading diagnostic, and direct operators to `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` for active QQBot state.

options.title: Add a narrow legacy override
options.body: Define `QQBOT_DATA_DIR` only for legacy imports and QQBot temporary downloads, validate it as a nonblank absolute path, and document that SQLite state is unaffected.

recommendation.title: Keep one state contract
recommendation.body: Remove the new variable, update the misleading diagnostic, and direct operators to `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` for active QQBot state.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged QQBot SQLite migration established the current storage boundary and explicitly treated this environment-variable work as separate.
